newsitem.title: GERMANY: U.S. Defence Secretary has "warm" talk with Kohl.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Defence Secretary has "warm" talk with Kohl.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen on Wednesday had what he called "very warm" discussions in Bonn with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on NATO and the American troop presence in Germany and Europe.

Cohen told reporters flying with him to Stuttgart after the 45-minute meeting that Kohl had expressed satisfaction with progress on NATO enlargement and urged a continued presence of American forces in Germany, where the United States now has about 75,000 troops.

"It was very good, a very warm period. We have a very cordial conversation," Cohen said, adding that Kohl expressed pleasure at Cohen's recent appointment as Defence Secretary because Cohen had long been interested in European affairs as a former U.S. senator.
"He thinks it's important that people be involved who have an understanding of U.S.-German relations certainly, but all of NATO," Cohen said.

"We discussed several key things. He feels it is very important that the United States maintains its presence in Germany and in Europe," the secretary said. "He knows that from time to time there are members (of the U.S. Congress) who call for a reduction of U.S. forces, but he wanted me to know how important it was for the United States to remain engaged."

Cohen said Kohl had also stressed the importance of the upcoming U.S.-Russia summit in Helsinki between Presidents Bill Clinton and Boris Yeltsin because of the need to move forward on Washington-Moscow relations.
